# Setup Lab

<!-- arlotope:contract (generated by `arlo docs` from workflow/) -->
**First, load the brief:** `uv run --with pyyaml python arlo.py brief setup-lab [--study <slug>]`; skip when `ARLOTOPE BRIEF /setup-lab` is already supplied. Follow its task ownership, additions and checkpoints.
<!-- /arlotope:contract -->

Optional configuration conversation. **New study** works without this skill. Configure only what
the PI needs now; retain unanswered settings and reuse preferences already given.

## Establish the useful settings

Read `lab/config.yaml`, `lab/RESEARCH.md` when present, and `docs/configuration.md`. Ask one focused
question at a time, using the harness's question tool or ending the turn with the question. Do not
re-ask information found in supplied briefs, repositories or previous answers.

- **Research:** current interests and the next question. Record useful directions in RESEARCH.md
  or OPEN-QUESTIONS.md; do not turn every interest into a study automatically.
- **Projects:** keep `lab.projects_root` or use the requested folder. Existing repositories can
  be attached without adopting the generated project scaffold.
- **Agents:** use an installed Claude, Codex, opencode or ACP-compatible agent. Installation,
  sign-in, named presets and launch permissions belong in **Settings → Agents & models** and
  **Limits & permissions**. Do not request passwords or API-key values in chat, invent model IDs
  or enable launches yourself. Optional child-agent tiers may stay `inherit`; use role_sync after
  an authorized tier/role change rather than editing generated files.
- **Depth and compute, when relevant:** offer the configured budget profiles from `tools/profiles.py list`,
  then ask only about needed compute concurrency, budget and oversight choices. Show a profile diff
  before applying it. Profile settings scale exploration, not integrity floors. Project budgets still
  come from the project's proposal; never invent them here.
- **Papers, when relevant:** ask the target venue and page limit. Use the configured venue files;
  do not impose paper settings or a TeX installation on a study that produces another deliverable.
- **Machine constraints, when relevant:** record the PI's data locations, scheduler rules and other
  instructions in `lab/SYSTEM.md` from its template. Do not create an empty constraints document.

The PI can adapt workflows and checkpoints under **Workflow**. Configuration keys do not define
those tasks or grant approval. Point out that option when relevant rather than requiring another setup interview.

## Apply and verify

Use `/configure`'s tools to apply the authorized values in the correct layer, preserving comments.
Inspect the resolved settings afterward and run `tools/check_lab.py`. Check Git/uv or a required
project tool only when the next action needs it. Report missing tools plainly; ask before installations
the PI has not requested. Documentation builds and disposable template test runs are developer checks,
not required onboarding work.

Record the changes in the notebook. Summarize only what changed, what is missing and one next action:
create/attach a study, run the requested procedure, or choose the already-authorized campaign.
`/advance` is the one-procedure pace; `/autopilot` requires an approved campaign brief.
